title: Associated-log quotient presheaf and presentation on an arbitrary scheme
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $R$ be a commutative monoid, and let $\beta:R\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a monoid homomorphism. On the small etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], write $\beta_W$ for restriction to $B_W=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$, $E_W=\beta_W^{-1}(B_W^\times)$ and $Q_\beta(W)=R\oplus_{E_W}B_W^\times$. This is the quotient of $R\times B_W^\times$ by the congruence generated by $(re,b)\sim(r,\beta_W(e)b)$, using the chart pushout of [def-trf-log-regular-pair] applied to the range restriction of $\beta_W$. For a morphism $f:V\to W$, restriction on pairs sends $(r,b)$ to $(r,f^\sharp b)$ and induces restriction on this quotient. These are the objects and maps of the commutative-monoid presheaf $Q_\beta$. No local Noetherian, finite generation or integrality hypothesis is imposed.

For a log structure $L$ with structural map $\alpha$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] and a natural monoid map $\eta:Q_\beta\to L$, define $\operatorname{IsAssociatedLogPresentation}(\beta,L,\eta)$ to mean that $\eta$ presents $L$ as the monoid sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]: for every commutative-monoid sheaf $H$, composition with $\eta$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(L,H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Q_\beta,H)$; and for every $W$, $r\in R$, and $b\in B_W^\times$ one has $\alpha_W(\eta_W([r,b]))=\beta_W(r)b$. This is a predicate on the given $L,\eta$, not an assertion that such data exist. Define its canonical global chart by $\iota(r)=\eta_X([r,1])$.

At a geometric point $t$ with strict local ring $A=\mathcal O_{X,t}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], define the stalk chart $\beta_t:R\to A$ as $\beta$ followed by the strict-local germ map of [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. For independent coefficient and site universes, transport $R$ by the canonical multiplicative down map $\operatorname{ULift} R\to R$: $\beta_W$, the global compatibility chart and $\beta_t$ are precomposed with this map, so their formulas on lifted elements are unchanged.

from.place: Proof Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality, regular finite-torsion local model; pointwise purity and composition used to compare the normalized curve with the ambient regular scheme. Input: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair. More precisely: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph. Specifically: XVI 3.7, p.255: 'Le log-schema X''' est regulier et log-lisse sur T', in the uniformizer-chart form required by Theorem 3.6.2 via Proposition 3.6.3. Internal chart argument: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3 proof, last paragraph, printed p.252, inverse-image monoid P=h^{-1}(M_x) and etale comparison; refinement of Kato (1988) Theorem 3.5 recalled in that paragraph. Auxiliary associated-log construction on the arbitrary infinitesimal test schemes in the prescribed-chart comparison argument. Definition of the quotient presheaf and its normalized associated-log presentation.
